normalization_or_editorial_flags.issue: Remove stray spaces before Arabic question marks.
Normalize initial conjunction spacing from 'و كيف' to 'وكيف'.
Mixed partial diacritization is inconsistent across the learner bank; define and apply one display policy rather than sporadic vowel marks.
Grammatical but stiff for everyday MSA; prefer a natural learner form such as هل أنت متفرغ غدًا؟ for 'Are you free tomorrow?'
Review أما زلت against the chosen punctuation/hamza convention for interrogative learner text.
صديقكِ can mean 'your friend' and does not unambiguously encode English 'boyfriend'; consider a clearer learner pair if relationship specificity matters.
Both are usable but صفاته/مواصفاته differ in naturalness for describing a person; native editorial review should pick the more learner-appropriate wording.
Future/present English phrasing is context-sensitive; tighten tense/aspect equivalence for standalone learner pairs.
Short لِمَ forms are inconsistently written without disambiguating vowel marks; for unvocalized beginner material, لماذا is often clearer.
Normalize punctuation spacing and Arabic comma conventions.
من أين تعرف/تعلم هذا is literal and less direct than كيف تعرف ذلك؟ for the English 'How do you know that?'; review learner naturalness.
ماذا تريد بعد؟ is less explicit for English 'What else do you want?'; consider ماذا تريد أيضًا؟ or ماذا تريد غير ذلك؟.
تقبل/توافق mean accept/agree rather than literally 'say yes'; decide whether to align English more literally or replace with a direct نعم construction.
نحن مجازون من المدرسة غدًا is understandable but stiff; prefer a more natural standalone learner sentence for 'We have no school tomorrow.'
